name: Space Shuttle Discovery
best_known_for: OV-103 — third operational Shuttle, deployed Hubble (STS-31, 1990), flew both return-to-flight missions after Challenger and Columbia. 39 missions, the most of any orbiter
credit: Third operational orbiter. First flight STS-41-D (1984-08-30) carried three commercial comsats. The most-flown Shuttle — 39 missions over 27 years, more than any other orbiter. Career highlights: STS-31 (1990-04-24) deployed the Hubble Space Telescope; STS-26 (1988-09-29) was the post-Challenger return-to-flight; STS-114 (2005-07-26) was the post-Columbia return-to-flight; STS-103 (1999-12) and STS-82 (1997-02) flew Hubble servicing missions 2 + 3A; STS-95 (1998) returned Senator John Glenn to orbit at age 77; STS-92 and STS-120 + STS-124 + STS-128 + STS-131 + STS-133 contributed to ISS assembly. Final flight STS-133 (2011-02-24) delivered the Leonardo Permanent Multipurpose Module. On display at the Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center (Smithsonian) since 2012-04.
